source.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
source.scope: Qwen and Llama finetuned on trait-eliciting and EM-like datasets (Normal, I, II)

tests.description: Finetune on many datasets; compute finetuning shift (projection of difference in mean last-prompt-token activations between finetuned and base on persona vector) and correlate with post-finetuning trait expression score; compare with cross-trait baselines.
tests.data: Evil, Sycophancy, Hallucination, Medical, Code, GSM8K, Math, Opinions datasets, versions Normal/I/II
tests.quote: We observe strong positive correlations ( r=0.76\text{--}0.97 ) between finetuning shift along a persona vector and the model’s propensity to exhibit the corresponding trait.

source_tests.description: Finetune on many datasets; compute finetuning shift (projection of difference in mean last-prompt-token activations between finetuned and base on persona vector) and correlate with post-finetuning trait expression score; compare with cross-trait baselines.

source.scope: Dataset-level and sample-level projection difference; synthetic datasets and LMSYS-Chat-1M plus three other real-world datasets

tests.description: Compute projection difference of training data (training responses vs base model responses) per dataset and correlate with post-finetuning trait expression.
tests.locator: Section 6.1, Figure 8, Appendices F, H, I
tests.metric: Correlation between projection difference and trait expression
tests.quote: dataset-level projection difference is highly predictive of post-finetuning trait expression.

tests.description: Compare projection histograms of samples from trait-inducing datasets vs Normal control datasets.
tests.data: Evil II, Sycophancy II, Hallucination II, Opinion Mistake II vs Normal
tests.quote: individual samples from trait-inducing datasets are highly separable from control samples based on their projection values onto persona directions.

tests.description: Finetune on top 500, bottom 500, and random 500 samples by projection difference from LMSYS-Chat-1M, with and without LLM-based filtering (score >1 removed); also three other real datasets.
tests.data: LMSYS-Chat-1M, Tulu 3 SFT Mixture, Ultra Chat 200k, WildChat
tests.quote: high projection difference samples induce the strongest trait expression, followed by random samples, and then low projection difference samples.

tests.description: Compare LLM judge filtering and projection-difference filtering on Opinion Normal + Mistake II mix, thresholds from Ultra Chat 200k 95th percentile.
tests.data: Opinion Normal+Mistake II; 20,000 Ultra Chat samples
tests.metric: Trait expression score after finetuning on 1,000 filtered samples, averaged over five runs
tests.quote: the combined filtering strategy consistently yields the best results across all traits

findings.statement: Personality shifts from finetuning can be mitigated with post-hoc intervention, or avoided with a new preventative steering method.
findings.question: q.chen2025
findings.quote: These shifts can be mitigated through post-hoc intervention, or avoided in the first place with a new preventative steering method.

source.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
source.scope: Qwen and Llama; inference-time steering and preventative steering during finetuning, evil/sycophancy/hallucination; MMLU and coherence

tests.description: Post-hoc inference-time steering against the persona vector in finetuned models with increasing coefficients, measuring trait expression, MMLU and coherence.
tests.metric: Trait expression score; MMLU accuracy; coherence
tests.quote: As the steering coefficient increases, the expression of the target trait decreases significantly.

tests.description: Preventative steering: add persona vector during finetuning; compare with inference-time steering, CAFT, regularization, multi-layer steering.
tests.quote: We observe that this strategy effectively reduces training-induced persona shifts, while also maintaining an average coherence score across all models above 80.

tests.description: Steering preserves domain-specific learned behavior; comparison with prompt-based mitigation; benign-data side effects; fact-acquisition case study with 1,000 new facts.
tests.locator: Appendix J.1, J.2, J.6, J.7, Figures 24, 25, 29, 30, 31
tests.data: Mistake GSM8K II, Mistake Medical II, Medical (Normal), 1,000 new facts
tests.metric: Trait score, domain behavior, MMLU, new-fact accuracy
tests.quote: preventative steering only slightly reduces new-fact accuracy while largely preserving MMLU performance.
